Subject: Clarify VAT treatment for NobleSoft (CH) invoices and PO setup

Hi Sergio —

Thanks for taking a look. We're starting the vendor onboarding for NobleSoft AG (Swiss legal entity) and want to make sure invoices and the PO flow are set up correctly. A few practical questions from our finance/tax team: 

- We are a Swiss VAT-registered company. For B2B SaaS supplied to Redwood (US-headquartered), do you require us to include Swiss VAT on invoices, or would Redwood prefer an invoice net of VAT with reverse-charge instructions?
- If reverse-charge is acceptable, can you confirm the billing entity and VAT ID Redwood wants on the vendor record? Redwood has EEA presence in some cases — please confirm which billing entity will receive the invoice so we can zero-rate exports where appropriate.
- Bank / remittance: do you require beneficiary name exactly as in the PO? Any mandatory PO fields we should include on the invoice (e.g., Redwood PO number, cost center)?

I've attached: VAT_certificate_NobleSoft_20270310.pdf (VAT registration in CH), SwissTaxRep_Letter_20270309.pdf (local tax representative for EU OSS queries), and a sample invoice.

Quick background: NobleSoft is SaaS (multi-tenant) hosted in AWS eu-west-1. Services are provisioned to Redwood's application team, billed monthly. We want to avoid issuing VAT where not required but will follow Redwood's preferred flow.

Can you loop in procurement/finance guidance? Happy to jump on a short call.

Hi Armin — thanks for the attachments, that helps. Short answer and then next steps.

Summary / preferred flow (procurement + finance standard):
- If Redwood is the billed entity in the US (Redwood Inc., US tax resident) we typically accept invoices net of CH VAT for cross-border services where vendor can demonstrate export/zero-rate treatment. In practice we need: vendor VAT certificate + a statement on the invoice that the supply is "export of services / zero-rated under CH VAT rules" or a standard reverse-charge phrase.
- If Redwood will be billed to an EU-registered Redwood legal entity (e.g., Redwood EU SARL or similar), we can apply reverse-charge (VAT not charged by vendor) only if Redwood supplies an EU VAT ID to the vendor. 
- Where the vendor insists on charging CH VAT, Redwood Finance can remit but Redwood will need the VAT invoice to be valid for reclaim (i.e., vendor VAT reg number and correct address).

Required onboarding items from NobleSoft to create the vendor record and PO: 
1) Completed vendor onboarding form (PDF/Docx) — please use this link and attach to reply (we've pre-filled some fields from your docs).
2) Company legal name + address exactly as on bank account.
3) Copy of Swiss VAT certificate (you provided) and statement whether the supply is exported services.
4) Bank details (IBAN/BIC) and confirmation if beneficiary name matches legal name.
5) W-8BEN-E: Redwood is US-based; our accounts payable team requires a W-8BEN-E for many non-US vendors even when not strictly US-source income — please provide completed form.
6) Sample invoice showing where PO number will appear.

PO fields we require on invoices: PO#, invoice date, invoice number, description of services, period covered, net amount, VAT amount (if charged), and bank wiring instructions. The PO will be issued once the vendor record is created (usually 3-5 business days after we receive complete docs).

Notes/edge cases: 
- If you want to zero-rate the invoice as an export from Switzerland, include the phrase "export of services — zero-rated under Swiss VAT" and we will provide a billing entity to support that.
- If you need Redwood's EU VAT ID for reverse-charge, we need to confirm which Redwood legal entity will receive the invoice (I will check with Laura on whether EU billing is available for this supplier).

Next steps: Please complete the attached vendor form (I pre-filled where possible) and return the W-8BEN-E + bank confirmation. I'll follow up with Laura on the EU/VAT ID path and get back to you by tomorrow COB.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Procurement Manager — Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
